title: Ramayana: Part 1 — Critics Hail Nitesh Tiwari's Epic as a Visual Masterpiece
excerpt: A stunning retelling of the ancient epic, though pacing and music draw mixed reactions.
body:
• Nitesh Tiwari's adaptation of Ramayana is visually stunning and ambitious.
  • Ranbir Kapoor and Yash deliver strong performances, particularly Yash as Ravana.
  • Critics praise the film's grand scale but note uneven pacing and a lack of emotional depth.
  • The film's musical score has received mixed reviews, impacting its emotional resonance.
  • Available in Hindi with subtitles, it's a significant cultural experience for the diaspora.

Opening

Nitesh Tiwari's ambitious adaptation of the ancient Indian epic, Ramayana: Part 1, has finally hit theaters, and critics are buzzing with excitement. This Hindi-language film, which stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Yash as Ravana, and Sai Pallavi as Sita, aims to bring the legendary tale of good versus evil to a contemporary audience with grand visuals and a sweeping narrative. Early reviews suggest that while the film excels in its visual storytelling and performances, it stumbles in pacing and musical composition.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=T0Uduwg2W2w

Critics from both Indian and international outlets have praised the film's scale, likening its epic proportions to that of Hollywood blockbusters. Taran Adarsh from Bollywood Hungama describes it as “nothing short of magnificent,” while NDTV calls it “one of 2026's most immersive cinematic experiences.” However, some critics express concerns about the film's pacing and emotional depth, suggesting that the spectacle sometimes overshadows the storytelling.

The consensus

With a blend of praise and critique, Ramayana: Part 1 has garnered an average rating of 3.5 out of 5 across various reviews. Critics largely agree on the film's visual grandeur and the strong performances from the lead actors, particularly Yash's portrayal of Ravana. However, there is a noticeable divide in opinions regarding its pacing and musical elements, with some reviewers arguing that these aspects detract from the overall experience. The film's reception appears to be more favorable among Indian critics, who celebrate its cultural significance, while some Western reviewers highlight its shortcomings in storytelling.

What's praised

One of the standout features of Ramayana: Part 1 is its breathtaking visual effects and cinematography. Critics from Esquire India commend the film for its “immersive cinematic scale,” drawing comparisons to epic franchises like The Lord of the Rings. The film's set designs and landscapes have been described as “vast” and “stunning,” creating a rich backdrop for the story. Ranbir Kapoor's performance as Lord Rama has also been highlighted as a career-defining role, with critics noting his ability to convey both strength and vulnerability.

Yash's portrayal of Ravana has received particular acclaim, with many reviewers praising his commanding presence and depth of character. Mint notes that Yash “steals the show” in several key scenes, bringing a nuanced performance that adds complexity to the traditional villain role. Sai Pallavi's depiction of Sita has also been well-received, with critics acknowledging her ability to embody grace and strength amidst adversity.

What's criticized

Despite its many strengths, Ramayana: Part 1 is not without its flaws. Critics have pointed out that the film's pacing can be uneven, particularly in the second half, where some scenes feel drawn out and detract from the narrative momentum. MensXP mentions that while the visuals are captivating, the film occasionally sacrifices emotional depth for spectacle, leaving some viewers wanting more from the character arcs and relationships.

Additionally, the film's musical score has drawn mixed reviews, with some critics feeling that it fails to resonate with the epic nature of the story. The songs, while melodious, are described as lacking the emotional punch needed to elevate key moments in the narrative. This has led to a sentiment that the film, while visually stunning, may not fully engage audiences on an emotional level.

What this means for you

For the Indian diaspora, Ramayana: Part 1 offers a chance to reconnect with a beloved cultural narrative, presented in a grand cinematic format. The film is available in Hindi with subtitles, making it accessible for non-Hindi speakers. Given its ambitious scope and the star power of its cast, it’s a must-see for fans of epic storytelling. With a runtime of approximately 180 minutes, audiences should prepare for an immersive experience that, despite its pacing issues, promises to be a visual feast.
